data.text:
No hazard requiring action.

All 5 sensors checked and trusted (none flat/stuck). S3 +1.2C residual plus S1/S2 slightly high and M1 up to ~3.5-4.0kW is explained by Rack B load ~1.27x nominal starting ~22 min ago. M2 voltage-drop rise 43mV to ~101mV is consistent with higher Rack B current.

Physics diagnosis: load_rackB posterior 1.0. Hidden-zone estimate: Rack B 29.3C +/-2C, limit 35C, margin 5.7C.

Forward simulation 60min: breach probability 0 with and without action, peak margin ~-5C well within limits. Power-cap and load-shed tested - only ~0.3C improvement, no breach-risk reduction, so safety-gate action not justified.

Conclusion: benign load increase, no limit breach plausible. Take no action, continue routine monitoring.

data.text:
No limit breach predicted — no automated action taken.

- All 5 sensors trusted (none flat; std normal).
- S1 +1.4C, S1/S3 trending up ~0.12-0.14C/10min last 90min; M1/M2 no sustained load/voltage anomaly.
- Physics twin: AC cooling degrading up to 60% loss, onset ~47 min ago, posterior 1.0. Hidden-zone regression: rackB 30.7±2C, margin 4.3C to 35C limit.
- If nothing done (60-90min): p_breach 0, expected peak margin -3.3C, worst -2.4C; p=0.8 to stay within 3C alert margin.
- Tested: backup cooling rackA (-3.3 to -3.7C), shed noncritical load (-3.3 to -4.0C), human check (no effect in horizon). Both technical actions help slightly under all AC variants, but breach risk is already 0, so no urgency to cut power or cap.
- Info notification sent. Recommend routine HVAC inspection for AC degradation, continue monitoring.
